The checkpoint placement predates the shallow graft; prepareContinuation (46ab36a4) and beforeRequest were added after it and widened the window, which is the strongest case for a latent reading.

That is filesystem behavior at large tree sizes, not a line that broke, so no in-repo commit can be quoted as the cause. One could argue #202197 (58dbe4055043) was an incomplete fix, but it never claimed to cap reservations ('not a calibrated btrfs transaction or latency limit'), so I don't name it as the cause.

The CLI's fixed scope requests (operator.read for gateway call, admin/read/write/approvals for the TUI) were correct for the operator grants they were written for; they broke only once session-only guest grants (operator.sessions.*) became a recommended setup, a usage the CLI never promised to support. This is a performance improvement of measured autosizing that was never faster: the repeated layout reads were the long-standing behavior (related issue #154271 and superseded PR #154272 predate it, and the PR says the cost remained 'even after #186874'), and no commit is shown to have made appending slower. The transcript candidate resolver has always used safeRealpathSync/existsSync (code older than the graft); 59d9759d0250 (#200136) converted only the final existence check in readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync to async and left the resolver synchronous, so this PR completes a zero-sync-filesystem hardening rather than repairing a behavior that ever worked differently. GraphQL blame of the pre-Solid talk-page.ts/talk.ts shows the catch-to-unavailable mapping and the 'Connect to the Gateway' unavailableHint both came from the original Talk settings page commit 7a1aa4eb (#115409); the Solid migration b8d31e96129 and the async-boundary refactor b79c32a97f88 (Errored fallback to kind unavailable) carried the same conflation forward, so it never distinguished failures from disconnection. The completion row was created in 18136c960eaf (#198133) with a generic bot icon, before any avatar component existed; the SubagentName avatar was added four days later by 69eb76e6347 (#201407) to launch/activity rows only. The accounting rule (sum serialized_bytes over context_eligible=1, where transcriptEventContextEligibility returns 1 for custom entries) and the openclaw.system-prompt checkpoint writer (session-prompt-state.ts) both predate the 2026-09-03 graft; the later actor counters (c9e7c71c0859 #171448, 87ca2c83893c #174274) only copied the existing SQL semantics, so none of them is a regression. The only effect is on the completeness of startup diagnostics that the performance collector harness reads, which is internal measurement tooling, not product behavior (the PR also notes that main's readiness does not even wait for post-attach, so the release regression test could not be ported). The fix extends the existing strict-policy redirect-inspection requirement (requiresInspectableBrowserNavigationRedirectsForUrl, which already gated the raw CDP fallback) to the Chrome MCP existing-session transport, closing an audit-found SSRF policy gap with no linked user report. The model-wait progress projection added in 8e02fdeaaa2e (#172951) was designed for waiting_for_model phases (local model responses and slot waits) and never covered provider retries; the fix adds a new progress notice for a new phase rather than restoring behavior that once worked. Nothing failed: typing was shown and the final answer arrived, so this is a UX enhancement framed as a fix.

The headline hang comes from the interrupted-update recovery path added in 59834998f25 (#165863): it stops forward command scopes on a signal during verifying and runs the restart/verification inside such a scope, but the readiness poller (its signal line dates from 2b125389c8b, Sept 22, before this commit) never read the scope signal, so every systemctl spawn died and polling continued until the deadline; that feature shipped with the bug. The second defect (admission using prepared.timeoutMs, unset by default, so a fixed 120 s) dates from acffa7681f0 (#155632) and is a separate never-worked sizing issue not traced further here.

The connect snapshot had restricted resolved paths (stateDir/configPath) to admin callers since 676b748056b (#58469, April 2026), and system.info was added later in 2bed3947937 (#100478, July 2026) with `diskPath: stateDir` exposed to read-only callers (GraphQL blame of the fix parent puts the diskPath line on that commit); e242a92f607 (#136079) later added the stateDir disks[] fallback with the same exposure. The defect shipped with the RPC, though it was found by audit rather than reported by a user, hence medium confidence.

The PR is a performance optimization measured on a synthetic inventory (metadata edit CPU 67 to 28 ms) with no reported failure and no claim that the work was ever cheaper; the redundant checks accumulated across the feature commits blamed (bf90074c33e2, 4f9aa4c9354a, 526371eefd46) rather than being broken by one. The second commit only keeps the PR's own change from altering requester order, which was not a defect on main.

The removed default-options ISO8601DateFormatter parsing is older than the graft; full-history listing shows the services landed on main in #11756 (6aedc54, after an earlier revert), and its diff (via gh api) contains the same `ISO8601DateFormatter()` + `formatter.date(from:)` parsing in Calendar, Motion and Reminders services. The fix changes model-facing guidance text to steer agent behavior (fewer polls, one waiter per result); the exec/process machinery itself behaved as coded, and the incident is a model choosing to poll under the old wording. The one factual mismatch (a wake promise for hidden subagents with no wake target, and wait guidance that ignored the 120 s yieldMs cap) is a small part of a prompt-tuning change, so I classify the whole as a guidance/behavior change rather than tracing a causing commit.

The removed lines blame to the Lit-to-Solid ports of October 2026; I checked the pre-port Lit file at 30469f45^ and the subtitle and value sat on separate lines of an html template literal, so whitespace rendered, and the JSX port dropped it. This is a performance improvement measured on a synthetic 35 GiB database: the OR-combined read query (from the #171336 usage rework, d2ef45ce) and the 30-second TTL for detail reports were never faster, and no functional failure or reported incident with a prior faster state is cited. The sibling delete path had already been switched to per-range indexed probes in #199374, and this extends the same optimization to reads, so it fits the rubric's performance-improvement-of-code-never-slower case.

Native launch-error attribution worked with the 0.164 launcher (spawn-style exit-1 diagnostics, #154489/#161419); the PR names #200784 as related, and that commit's diff bumps Codex to 0.169.0 (an execve-based launcher) while adding only the Node 26 structured execve branch, so on Node 24 the diagnostic was lost and the real-launcher tests failed in the hourly Codex shard right after. The PR describes a deliberate presentation redesign: the old chat-message acknowledgments worked as designed (from the update run/report features in #138690/#138737), and the fix adds a new noticeSurface field, toast UI and i18n strings rather than repairing broken behavior. The PR frames itself as bounded waste removal measured against a benchmark, with output byte-for-byte unchanged and no reported failure or earlier faster state; it names no commit that made streaming slower. Blame of every removed assertPrivate line points to 3c34fff (#146616), which created update-candidate-plugin-repair.ts and the private-only target assertion; at that commit update-candidate-plugin-tree.ts already projected host links to the candidate root (`relocations.push({ sourceRoot: host, destinationRoot: candidateRoot })`, `hostLinks`), so the conflict existed from the start. The removed condition sits in session-thinking-claims.ts, created by the refactor 1ad9fe2 (#143049), but that code was moved verbatim from ui/src/lib/sessions/index.ts, where GraphQL blame attributes the claim logic including the delete branch to f49742b (#125822). Agent commands writing to the OS default /tmp is standard behavior that OpenClaw never claimed to manage; the 24-hour scratch expiry feature (99ba844a3cd5, #193677) only covered workspace scratch by design, and this PR extends that policy by redirecting temp environment variables, a new default rather than restoring broken behavior. Blame candidates are the scratch-expiry feature and unrelated sandbox/CLI env plumbing that the change rewires, none of which broke temp routing.

git log -S sessionScope on session-menu-access.ts shows #155184 introduced the narrow own-session write path and in the same diff opted label/pin into it while leaving icon/color reasons unscoped, so appearance never worked for scoped writers; the runtime dispatchers likewise never passed sessionScope for appearance. Confidence is low because #155184's description only promised rename/pin/archive/restore, so the omission may have been scope rather than a bug, and the secondary Discord account-selection issue dates from #188910 (4674051ce50a), its own introduction.

The PR states it is diagnostics only: refusal behavior, authorization, eligibility and user notice are unchanged, and the previous code deliberately returned undefined for these cases. Adding detail to a log payload is an observability improvement, not a fix of broken behavior, so no causing commit applies.

This is a performance improvement measured against a baseline; the transient rebuild came from the long-standing loader-based redirect design (blame points to the original settings routes, the shallow graft, and #150133), not from a commit that made navigation slower than before. A sibling perf change hours earlier (#194624) applied the same treatment to General settings, consistent with an optimization series rather than a regression fix.

git log -S 'outputText === undefined' shows the check entered with the original full-output recovery in #153542 (Lit chat-tool-output.ts) and was carried verbatim into the Solid view by #168739 (75df19cf9e4) and later refactors, so the misclassification of text-less results shipped with the feature. Medium confidence because I did not confirm image-only MCP results reached this view at the time #153542 landed, though the PR says they come from existing MCP content conversion.

This is the third mitigation in two days (#202197 pacing, #202563 reservation watermark, now commit-latency and pass bounds) of the same host I/O load from background deletion; each step tightened the pacing, and none made deletion heavier than before. No earlier commit made cleanup interfere more, so there is no regression to cite: it is an iterative performance tuning of background cleanup (the PR calls it a mitigation, not a guarantee), closest to a performance improvement of code that was never better.

terminalAnswer's `join(", ") || answered` logic dates to the July ask_user work (d7de67ae) and was carried unchanged through the Solid port (a5832a9b3866); at that time empty answers were not accepted. Medium because I did not confirm that the Control UI panel could submit an empty answer at exactly that commit; it could be read as latent with that commit as trigger.

The PR states the inventory flags and list format were removed by the upstream OpenShell v0.1.3 CLI, an external tool contract change; the plugin code was written against the older CLI. The in-repo trigger is the dependency refresh 0320b94b (#174410), which bumped the CI E2E pin from v0.1.2 to v0.1.3 without adjusting the calls; for users the break came from installing the newer OpenShell, not from a repo commit.

The fix adds a liveness bound that the attempt never had; blame candidates are only context lines, and no earlier commit removed a startup deadline, so this is not a regression. The failure needs the hosted native service to stall without emitting events, an external service behavior the code relied on the outer watchdog to bound. It could also be read as never-worked (the attempt shipped without a first-event bound in the September 2026 Agents API work), but no single introducing line plainly causes it.

None of the three comparisons ever normalized Unicode, so the gap is effectively never-worked, but it spans three independent surfaces each written separately, and blame failed on missing objects, so no single introducing commit can be named. Nothing suggests a regression: the removed lines only lowercased.

Before 3d7f8fbf (#182516) nested Agents/Workflows with a parent_task_id were owner=false and never held; that commit introduced holding children of held parents, with the parent-held check evaluated in one pass in snapshot order, which is exactly the ordering defect fixed here. Intervening commits (c93890f, etc.) only renamed calls to tasks.*; the PR body confirms main's scan was single-pass.

This is a performance optimization in a series (#194475, #196835) of reconciliation-stall reductions: the main-thread serialization of the rollback pack was the original design, not something a later commit made slower, and the PR's own benchmark shows 60 ms segments reduced to 8 ms without reproducing the reported 1.1 s production stall. Per the rubric, a performance improvement of code that was never faster is not-a-defect; no causing commit is identified.

PR #196942 describes itself as a requested UI/Read aloud rollback of #196602 ('Requested by' a maintainer), not a fix for a reported malfunction; the diff is the exact inverse of 685f18a's UI hunks. Reverting a presentation choice is a product decision, so not-a-defect.

The PR states no user impact for normal use and no bundled client sends the mark; the only effect was a self-inflicted abortable wait on the caller's own input, so this is hardening without a reported failure. No causing commit was traced since it is not classified as a defect.

The MCP loopback caller's only route for the turn's abort was the receiptAuthority boolean (isGrantAndLineageCurrent, which includes the grant's abort signal); adb2f7c (#203487) deliberately stopped calling that boolean synchronously, leaving only approvalSignals, which mcp-http.ts did not populate. The fix PR states the Stop test was red on main and passed before #203487 (with the generic authority text), and #203487's diff shows the removed check.

The exact restore-time compare `generationOwner.requiredGeneration !== snapshot.sharedGeneration` dates from 961f5c0b7099 (#166553), written for short-lived restart recovery of an in-flight turn, where refusing after a proxy policy change is a reasonable 'start a new user turn'; the trusted-proxy generation hash (proxy admission settings) predates the graft. d74a4aeb7d6 (#176422) began persisting that recovery source in long-lived cron jobs, which relied on the generation staying stable for weeks, and an external deployment change (Enterprise controller adding requiredHeaders) exposed it, so this reads as latent rather than a regression with a quotable breaking line.

The raw-identity automatic gate came from ff6f58a (#169038), before remount settlement existed; c66da3d (#170046) introduced the verified remount mapping for settlement but applied it only below that gate, so automatic settlement never handled a remounted journal (the PR's regression tests fail on base). 0679b18 (#181307) later widened automatic settlement to interrupted updates but kept the same gate; I attribute to c66da3d as the PR does, with medium confidence because c66da3d deliberately routed remount recovery through repair and which automatic path the reporter hit is not fully confirmed.

The raw runtime version in the OpenAI attribution `version` header is long-standing and was harmless until ChatGPT began gating new subscription models (gpt-6.2) on minimal client version, an external backend change; #202380 (7d1d7d035ce6) only normalized the listing side and explicitly left the turn header unchanged, so it did not break turns that previously worked. Evidence is thin: the failure for beta/dev values is inferred from a live 0.164.0 probe and unit tests, not a reported user failure, so this is a low-certainty latent call.

The in-chat automation card and its exact-job watcher were introduced in fc58825c81bd, which treated every read failure, including not-found for a deleted job, as retryable and showed Retry; c9cc12844c7d later restructured the card but kept the same `retryable` handling. No earlier version behaved correctly, so it is never-worked with fc58825c81bd as cause (its subject carries no PR number).

The change adds two informational fields to an existing JSON report; deletion behavior, human output and the stderr notice that already disclosed the sidecar coverage are unchanged, so nothing that previously worked broke and no command produced wrong results. It is an additive reporting improvement, which the rubric treats as not-a-defect; with no removed lines there was no causing code to trace.

The intentional_non_delivery disposition for source_owner_changed predates the 2026-09-03 graft (c61ba3ea5d26 only extracted it into sourceOwnerChangedResult) and was a deliberate choice under the older policy that dropped results when the source owner changed. It became wrong when the subsystem moved to 'finished results are always delivered or noticed' (#200760 removed the store-path and authority refusals but left this classification), so I treat it as latent with that policy change as trigger rather than a regression; it could also be read as a policy change, so this is a judgment call. I could not trace the pre-graft introducing commit.

The unqualified .where("owner", "=", key) was written in 339c4da81f54 (#164938) against node:sqlite's DatabaseSync, where it resolves to the target row and works. It broke only once the worker ran on PostgreSQL, where the name is ambiguous with EXCLUDED; #171521 (1edc42ce552) switched this function to the engine-neutral EngineConnection handle without changing the SQL, exposing it to PostgreSQL. Since the SQL was correct for SQLite, its only engine at the time, I classify it as latent with the engine-neutral change as trigger, not a regression.

loadSkillsStatusReport never passed an abort signal; the call shape predates the 2026-09-03 graft (3949fc0850e5 and 08f4a198a310 only refactored and moved it), and skills-cli.ts first used getAsyncWorkSignal on the same day as this fix (#198163 for skills update). The cooperative signal-exit machinery (src/cli/signal-exit-barrier.ts, async-work-scope.ts) is also older than the graft, so I could not tell whether these reads were written without cancellation from the start (never-worked) or were exposed when SIGINT handling became cooperative (latent), and I could not identify either commit.

Before ba6dce8d054d, selected human mentions did not suppress the agent, so requests with a cc mention were answered. That commit added isHumanAddressedChatMessage and wired chat.send to skip the agent turn whenever any person was selected and the agent was not named; its diff and docs ('A message with selected people is addressed to them, not to the agent') show the over-broad rule that suppressed cc'd requests, and the fix narrows it to leading mentions. The fix landed the day after, and ba6dce has no PR number in its subject.

Read via the GitHub commits API (pre-graft): #19424 (bfc9736) introduced the share extension with a 10-image activation rule but a 3-image send limit and no video sending; #20308 (c2d12b7e) later added NSExtensionActivationSupportsMovieWithMaxCount 1 while videos were still unsendable. Before #106513 (6e8df6c) the extra items were dropped silently; that commit made them a visible block without narrowing the activation rule. The mismatch shipped with the feature, so I classify it as never-worked with #19424 as cause; medium confidence because the video half came from #20308 and the blocked-sheet symptom from #106513.

The deferral feature and its stated guarantee that disposable rows are still removed both arrived in ac797242b03; its diff threaded deferArchiving through the planner, memory path and age/cap helpers but not the pre-existing SQLite cap candidate query (from 2ff5d6fbb21), whose oldest-first selection picked only durable rows that the planner then preserved. The fix's test (two older durable rows, one newer disposable, cap 1) shows exactly that, so the feature never worked on the SQLite path.

This is a bounded, one-time memory retention reduction (13-14 MB on a 35 GiB synthetic fixture) with no reported failure; the PR itself says it does not explain long-running growth and claims no other behavior change. The retained closure dates to restart input recovery (9bf3231d253, #187822) and was never lighter, so under the rubric this is a resource optimization rather than a defect; the blamed f787a896894 lines are only the unrelated assertion-helper refactor.
The PR fixes a production Knip unused-export failure left by #184512; production behavior is unchanged (0 production LOC delta). That is a tooling/lint fix titled as a fix, so not-a-defect.

The rejected call behaved as designed (the tool is not top-level and nothing executed); issue #179823 asks for recovery guidance in the error text, which this adds without changing permissions or the tool surface. That is a model-guidance/UX improvement rather than broken behavior, so not-a-defect; I did not trace the Code Mode introduction because no working state was lost.

GraphQL blame puts the fs.access(X_OK) probe (EPERM not tolerated) in b68c13660904 (#128370, 2026-08-25), where it is equivalent to a mode-bit check on an ordinary host and worked for its intended use. The fix a week later corrects how that newly added interrupted-recovery feature behaves, so the defects shipped with it.

The unwind file was created in 000af986 (#140339), whose admission-refusal catch formatted the pending failure from the refusal alone; later refactors (d780fdc, 16095df's pendingFailure helper) kept formatErrorMessage(cause) unchanged, so the first failure was never shown. Scratch expiry was added by 99ba844a (#193677, 2026-11-05) as paced main-thread streaming deletion, and it has always run on the Gateway thread; this change relocates that work to a worker for a measured performance gain rather than restoring earlier behavior or fixing incorrect results. Per the rubric, improving code that was never faster is not-a-defect, although the cost was user-visible as Gateway load.

At 1f3524e's parent, composer.css already drew the dictation border with `.agent-chat__input--dictating::after`, and the drop tint lived on the composer shell's own ::after. 1f3524e (#200758) retargeted the tint to `.agent-chat__input::after` with a more specific selector, so the tint rules replaced the border's styles; the fix PR describes the same mechanism and adds a red/green regression for it.

59b8a114 (#192345) introduced OpenClaw ID membership roles and applied them in resolveOperatorRolePolicy(client) and the run-authority capture, but authorizeGatewaySessionCreation's actor/profileId branch (resolveOperatorRolePolicyForProfile) used by session create/reset never consulted the membership policy, so the cap was missing from creation from the start. Later commits (07c8e14 linking, 4fc7acf member-role definitions) extended the feature without closing this path; confidence is medium because I did not confirm that the member-to-profile link path was reachable exactly as of 59b8a114.

The click-only retarget guard was introduced with the mobile composer gesture handling in 1bc029e (#176498), and b77c6de (#181021) began focusing the editor during pointerdown so the keyboard opens before touchend, which is what moves the composer under the finger before Chrome's compatibility mousedown. The frozen-batch gate requiring every member to be ready blames to d7381633 (#184022), but that commit only swapped an equivalent local `hasSettled` (which already rejected `sessions_yield`) for the shared `isRequesterSettleMemberReady`, so it is not the cause. The gate predates 4bf041c0 (#164154) and message waits date from d023e9f (#161114, 2026-09-29), with heavy churn of restart/owed-batch recovery since; I could not pin which commit first let a message wait sit in a frozen batch alongside ready siblings, so neither regression nor never-worked can be named with a cited line.

The lax check (regex plus `Number.isFinite(Date.parse(value))`) shipped unchanged with the plugin in e210870 (#165399); the fix adds stricter validation of untrusted remote input with no linked issue, reported failure or PR describing user impact. That is input-validation hardening rather than a defect anyone hit, so not-a-defect; if counted as a defect it would be never-worked in e210870.

The only file changed is apps/ios/UITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests.swift; the PR states app behavior and captured screens are unchanged and it only speeds up screenshot-test automation. A test-tooling performance change is not-a-defect under the rubric; the slow gutter tap came from af1b5e2 (#185676), which was a working (if slow) test step.

Blame of the removed override and selector lines points to 1655625f (#189537), whose diff adds exactly the transparent/muted override and adds the subagent avatar to the row-icon slot selectors; before it the avatars used the hue tint from chat-details-subagents.css. GraphQL blame puts the documentRevision epoch lines in tab-access.js on cbdce43b58a (#132232), whose diff split document freshness from access revocation in state but kept routing a stale document epoch through the existing `reason: "revoked"` path, so the diagnostic was wrong from the moment document-only invalidation existed. Before that commit every navigation called invalidateTab (full revocation), so the 'revoked' message was arguably accurate then; the bb702615dbf blame candidate only refactored the message table. Medium confidence because this is a diagnostic-wording defect and an earlier version also reported navigation as revoked.

Blame of the removed line and the feature diff show #161913 introduced the guard as a plain `new Error` on day one. At that commit the expected-error mechanism (isExpectedCliError/ExpectedCliError) already existed, runCommandWithRuntime already rethrew all errors in JSON mode, and formatCliFailureLines already gave non-expected errors the generic title plus `Try: openclaw doctor`. So the JSON-mode output was wrong from the start, and no later commit broke it.

Before 10d67445fbe, changed checkpoints paused and captured directly, which is the state this fix restores. That commit introduced a btrfs snapshot plus recursive removal for every changed checkpoint, and per the fix PR each snapshot forces a filesystem-wide btrfs transaction commit that stalled Gateway SQLite in production. d7f90ec35cf (#196727, retire captures, select snapshots only for large or slow trees) and 8ff37a6828b (#198128, skip the freeze) tuned the same path but kept snapshots for exactly the large workspaces that stalled. Medium confidence: the stall mechanism depends on btrfs kernel behavior and production timings I could not verify, and the fix is framed as an owner-accepted trade-off (about 290 ms of extra guest pause) rather than a pure bug fix.

The batch-wide failure comes from getSharedGatewayContextResolver throwing 'incompatible Gateway bindings: bound and unbound owners' for mixed batches. That throw is in gateway-context-binding.ts, which c69b8b98686 (#153508, an unrelated subject) created, and the -S search on its likely prior home in gateway-request-scope.ts timed out. Mixed batches also depend on separate gaps: restored rows lose their in-memory binding, and visible spawn did not capture the binding, from code I traced back to before the graft. The lost failure notice involves the yielded-batch path from #198807 and #163195. No single commit plainly introduced the failure, so I can't name a causing line with a straight face.

This is a performance and design change by the perf-loop lead: the PR calls advertising the last known schema during refresh an intentional trade-off. Before the fix, each new session runtime listed its servers under the existing bounded deadline. The removed code shows the catalog was cached only per runtime (`let lastListedCatalog` inside the runtime), with no evidence that new chats ever reused catalogs across runtimes. The blame candidates are older MCP lifecycle fixes, none of which made new chats slower, so no commit regressed this.

The ellipsis truncation was deliberate styling: the h3 nowrap/ellipsis rule dates from c1ecbca6ca50/d66f296eae1e, the shared Plugins row style (plugins.css .plugin-card-author and .plugin-catalog-results--rows h3) also ellipsizes, and the pre-rows card (before b8a06aa16af0) already capped the publisher at max-width 40%. The fix is a readability design change to wrap instead of truncate, not a repair of broken behavior.

GraphQL blame and the full-history log show the 'timeoutMs: Math.min(params.timeoutMs, 5_000)' cap was present from the file's creation in 1e0062b44a51 (#93446, June 2026); 2409cd6489b4 only reformatted it. The failure comes from the external Codex app-server's own best-effort 5-second catalog refresh (codex-rs models-manager) racing that cap, a dependency behavior I could not date relative to June, so latent fits better than never-worked; with no in-repo trigger identified, trigger_sha is null and this is a judgment call between latent and never-worked.

be2850e6d25e created the drain with an unbounded map over all stored sessions, and at that commit prepareSessionLifecycleDrain already did placement reads via readSessionWorkerPlacementAsync, whose getManyAsync runs on the shared state worker (runOpenClawStateWorkerOperation), so large histories could hit worker capacity from the start; bb4fa451b28e only wrapped the same fan-out with onPrepared/finished handling. Medium because I did not confirm the exact worker capacity cap at be2850e6, and the catalog-unavailability half of the fix may have a different origin that I did not trace.

Both proxy files were created in 59b8a114bf6d (#192345) and not touched again before the fix; that commit's ws-proxy.ts line 34 uses the ws+unix URL form, which mis-splits paths containing colons (the PR shows '/ws?session=agent:main:main' arriving as '/ws?session=agent'), and http-proxy.ts passed client framing headers through. The defects shipped with the feature, so never-worked.

The narrow-board rule that stacks cards at their saved row span is older than the graft and is commented as deliberate ('Keep desktop sizes canonical; only placement changes on narrow boards'), and scrolling inside a user-sized card is the intended desktop behavior that the fix keeps. The fix is a phone-layout design change rather than a repair of broken code; a case could be made for latent, exposed when native DOM reports (e90a3baabc14, #139306) grew much taller when stacked at phone width.

The PR is step 13/17 of a feature stack building invited-member session sharing; it adds a new owner operation rather than repairing a reported failure, and its own comparison shows main has no equivalent operation (mention-only control grants no membership by design). The blame candidates are the features this extends (#152083, #164484), not a breaking change, so this is new capability titled as a fix.

The socket-owned legacyCredentials projection was introduced inside DashboardWindowAuth's Equatable identity by #159860, which designed page retention only for the reconnect-before-retirement order; the fix PR reports the unchanged base fails the retirement-first case while the opposite order passes, so the defect shipped with that design rather than being broken later. Later commits (#161464) only refined the same-socket refresh path; local blobs were missing so the diff was read through the GitHub API, and the exact old-to-new comparison lines in DashboardManager could not be blamed, hence medium confidence.

The pre-fix accounting policy used a visitor with no early exit and deliberately counted every candidate event and scanned for leaf controls, so reading the whole 512-event tail was the design since the worker accounting move (#163045) and #190182 only fixed the limit constant; no commit removed an earlier early exit. This is a performance improvement of code that was never faster, with unchanged results, so it is not a defect.

The trailing-debounce writer subscribed to every Gateway, agent and session publication from its introduction in #141121, and the boot-record persist function has always cleared and re-armed the timer; the earlier #189738 only filtered session row publications, leaving Gateway/agent ones resetting the deadline. No later commit changed that subscription to break a working rule, so the defect shipped with the feature.

The retained-runtime generation (#153764, 2026-09-22) bound worker resolution through async context only, and the shared lease heartbeat carrier spawns workers via runInDetachedAsyncContext (present since at least #168807-era code in October); this was harmless as long as the updater's own dist stayed on disk, which still holds for npm and first pnpm installs. It broke only once the updater itself ran from a pnpm group-local virtual store that activation moves into the transaction backup, an install-layout situation produced by recent pnpm update work (#200366/#201735/#202017), but I could not pin which single commit first made activation move the running updater's group, so no trigger_sha is given.

Shell snapshot capture has used fs-safe's withTempWorkspace since before the graft (f06ffe2bbe4 only swapped the in-repo re-export wrapper of the same @openclaw/fs-safe/temp function for a direct import), so no in-repo commit changed the behavior. The freeze comes from the external fs-safe dependency performing its native creates synchronously, which only hurt under production btrfs commit contention; I could not tie it to a specific fs-safe version bump (0.26.14 to 0.28 bumps in Oct-Nov have no evidence of introducing sync native creates), so this is latent dependency/platform exposure rather than a regression.

The PR explicitly says it does not establish or fix the cause of the missing-answer incident and leaves runtime behavior unchanged; it only adds diagnostics gated on OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 and test-harness reporting. That is observability/test tooling titled as a fix, so not-a-defect.

The PR names two problems. The functional one, detailed model replies rejected for exceeding list limits, dates to the file's creation in c50ff4fbe54, which added the maxItems schemas without telling the model the limits or tolerating overflow, so it never worked. The UI duplication came from 9d4d6c62c06 (#177232), which registered both a header action and a session-header accessory a day earlier; removing them is partly a product direction (side panel only), so I cited the findings defect as the cause.

GraphQL blame at the pre-split loader.ts shows the lowercased manifest lookup came from de1d329e (June 2026, #93678); before it, 5fde14b's resolveDreamingSidecarEngineId only lowercased to compare against "none"/memory-core and the loader exempted memory-core via `pluginId !== dreamingEngineId`, which worked regardless of the selected ID's case. Later refactors (f1fc708f75c, a38b64b2fea5) preserved the lowercasing. Medium because I did not confirm the startup-planner side's history or that mixed-case declared IDs were preserved through slot normalization before June.

The whole-object `createMemo<PickerParams<...>>` was introduced by 0a32b78ba64 (#171882, Oct 15) and later reshaped by 4285c6ced42 (#191385, Nov 3, Continue-confirm flow for model-setup pickers with more than two options), while the Picker/select-picker internals that read `params.variant` changed in many commits since. The PR does not say when the transition last worked, and its own unit transition test passes on base, so I could not tie the undefined-params failure to the introducing commit, to 4285c6ced42, or to a Solid/picker change with a quotable line.

Citation redirect resolution already existed in runGeminiSearch when 1143f738423 ("fix(web-search): honor provider abort signals") added cancellation support for Gemini search; that diff threaded the signal into the main request only, so cancellation never covered citation fetches from the day it was introduced. Checked the file at 1143f738423 via the contents API (citation loop present, no signal) and the commit's patch; later commits in the local history are refactors that did not touch this. It is a missed path of the cancellation feature, not a later break, hence never-worked with medium confidence.

Before #193548 the materializer swept cache entries older than 24 hours on each archive read; bfbb6560585b (#193548, landed an hour earlier) removed both the writer and that sweep without a migration, leaving existing files permanently orphaned. I read the removed sweep in that diff; the fix is the missing cleanup for that cutover. Confidence is medium because one could also view this as a one-time cleanup (not-a-defect), but the pre-existing behavior of reclaiming old entries was removed by a specific commit.

Per-requester MCP servers never reached Claude CLI: before #172026 the native Claude path resolved OAuth with the operator identity and acquired the runtime without a requester, and only the Codex app-server called materializeRequesterScopedMcpToolsForHarnessRunCore (checked with git grep at 77d9f42c86bf^). #172026 introduced the loopback bridge for configured MCP with an explicit `requesterSenderId: undefined` and docs saying requester-scoped servers "are not offered on these turns", so the gap shipped with the path the fix repairs rather than breaking a working one. Medium confidence because the omission was deliberate and could also be read as a missing feature.

The macOS app's bundled Bun (since 271702bb8d8, #161709) relies on OPENCLAW_SQLITE_LIBRARY in the environment, and the read-only worker launch has built the child env from the request env since at least a06612710e6 (#167024), so a caller passing a limited env drops the library path. The subject says "restore", but the commit has no PR or body, and I could not identify which change started passing a projected env on the setup-detection path (candidates such as 9323fb9d1d2/#200192 rework credential reads but I could not confirm the mechanism). Without a quotable breaking line, the origin stays unclear.

The PR is a performance change that moves an unchanged read (same SQL and parser) out of the write transaction, backed by a synthetic benchmark rather than a reported failure, and claims no lower total latency. Nothing indicates a commit made deletion hold the lock longer than before, so it is a performance improvement of code that was not slower earlier, which the rubric classifies as not-a-defect.

The doctor feature (feat(browser): expose doctor diagnostics to agents, pre-graft, read via gh api) introduced the executable check that passes whenever an executable path is detected and the 'launchable' wording; no later commit changed that logic, so the misleading health report shipped with the feature. It is borderline with a diagnostic enhancement, hence medium confidence; the commit subject has no PR number.

The followup runner's catch-all (`try { assertCurrent() } catch { operatorAuthorityLost = true }`, present since at least the Oct 18 controller refactor) was correct while every assertCurrent failure meant revocation; #198245 introduced the non-revoking 'policy unavailable' error and taught only the owners about it, so outage survival for queued input never worked from that commit (#198729 later patched some steer/mailbox readers but not the followup runner or drain). It could also be read as latent with #198245 as trigger, hence medium confidence.

This is a performance optimization: the reader has selected both fingerprint columns since it was written (blamed to #184581), and the PR reports no failure and no measured production cost. Nothing became slower than before, so it is not a defect.

The production diff only changes error message text; every authority and revocation check is unchanged, and the PR states the triggering revocation was not attributed and is not claimed fixed. A copy change adding recovery guidance is not a defect under the rubric.

The event-driven re-read that floods history reads was added by #175025 (pending/access-denied/host-failure states) and fired for any widget without a view, including terminal unavailable errors; later refactors (#176457, #183467) only moved this logic into the loader/owner modules. The fix also bundles a server-side ordering optimization and a sandbox-failure classification, so the single cause is medium confidence.
